title: Pre-approved loan with advance fee vs. pre-approved offer with fees in the KFS
summary: A caller from Kaveri Bank offers the recipient a pre-approved personal loan. In the fraud case, the caller says the loan will be released only after the recipient pays a processing fee to a UPI ID the caller reads out. In the legitimate case, the caller describes the same offer, says the processing fee is listed in the Key Facts Statement and deducted from the loan amount, and tells the recipient to apply in the Kaveri Bank app or at a branch. Both callers name a processing fee.

shared_setting.pretext: a pre-approved personal loan of [AMOUNT_1] (₹50,000–₹5,00,000) with a processing fee of [AMOUNT_2] (₹1,000–₹10,000).
shared_setting.recipient_profile: an adult Kaveri Bank customer with a salary or business income; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Both callers say the offer is valid for a limited time and that approval is quick.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller requires an upfront fee to a caller-specified UPI ID before any disbursal. Genuine lenders deduct processing fees from the sanctioned amount and disburse only into the borrower's own account.
fraud.caller_objective: Get the recipient to send [AMOUNT_2] to [UPI_ID_1].
stable_facts: [UPI_ID_1] is presented as the "loan processing desk" but is not an account in the recipient's own name at Kaveri Bank.
The caller says the loan amount will reach the account "within an hour" of the fee.
The caller may send a "sanction letter" image by message. Its content is not evidence.

legitimate.label_rationale: The caller presents an offer, discloses the fee as part of the loan terms, and sends the recipient to official channels to apply. No payment is requested.
legitimate.caller_objective: Get the recipient to apply for the pre-approved loan through the app or branch.
stable_facts: The offer is visible in the "Loans" section of the Kaveri Bank app the recipient already uses.
The Key Facts Statement shown before acceptance lists the interest rate, annual percentage rate, and the processing fee.
The fee is deducted from the amount credited. The loan goes only into the recipient's own Kaveri Bank account.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may reduce the fee, add a "last chance", or give up. They must not switch to a different mechanism (for example asking for OTP, card details, or an app install). The legitimate caller must not ask for any payment, credential, or document by message after the branch.

must_preserve: loan amount and processing fee amount in both
fee deducted from loan and shown in KFS (_L)
may_vary: up to 2 filler turns before turn 3
must_not_emit: specific real interest rates presented as fact

ambiguities: Processing fee", its amount, and a time limit appear in both cases. The label depends on whether the fee must be paid separately to a caller-named payee before disbursal.
The catalog originally paired the fraud with an officer following up an applied loan. This card uses a pre-approved offer in both cases so the pretext is identical.
A genuine bank may charge other fees (stamp duty, insurance). They are also deducted or disclosed in the KFS. Generators must not invent a legitimate upfront fee.
An image of a "sanction letter" is not evidence either way.

evidence_references.claim: Processing fee is deducted from the sanctioned amount; banks never ask for an advance fee (CB09)
Loans are disbursed only into the borrower's own bank account (CB10)
Fees not in the KFS cannot be charged without explicit consent (CB11)
Fraud can be reported on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in (C12)
